claim: Changing the objective silently invalidates both of the optical tweezers' calibrations -- the GUI's pixel-to-micrometre magnification and the AOD's trapping-field response -- and neither is readable over TCP. Afterwards every commanded trap position in micrometres lands somewhere else and nothing reports it.
validity_conditions: Ruled TRANSFER under 10.2.1 and passed 10.3 rule 1, so it caps at E3 -- a run taken in another project is not a run taken here. 10.2's hardware-control-path row is open and says in its own rule that it does not wait for envelope/, because wrapping a control path needs no safety limit. Slot: A4 for the configuration change and O1 preflight for the check it forces, with A7 as the axis that owns commanded motion. It is the specific case of tweez300_reports_nothing_back that bites hardest, because the invalidating action is on a different device from the one that goes wrong. The check is to drive a known amplitude and measure it; the store holds no threshold for what counts as agreement, and that is a caller's judgement recorded in its plan.
